newsitem.title: INDIA: India Ranbaxy chief sees growth in merger.
newsitem.headline: India Ranbaxy chief sees growth in merger.

text.p: The chief of India's leading pharmaceutical firm Ranbaxy Laboratories Ltd said on Tuesday that a proposed merger with a small firm would help the company improve its domestic market share.
"We'll increase market share .... (through) a strategy of relationships, alliances," Parvinder Singh, chairman and managing director of Ranbaxy told reporters.

The boards of Ranbaxy and Croslands Research Laboratories Ltd on Monday decided to merge the latter with Ranbaxy with effect from April 1, 1996, subject to the approval of shareholders and the courts.
"It fitted in beautifully to have a relationship...the right kind of chemistry," Singh said.
Under the proposal, three Ranbaxy shares would be exchanged for every seven shares of Croslands.
The merged firm's market share would go up to 4.9 percent from Ranbaxy's current 3.9 percent, the company said.
"The addition of Croslands product range will also supplement Ranbaxy's export effort," a press statement said.
Croslands specialises in skincare drugs, while Ranbaxy leads in antibiotics with about 50 percent of its earnings coming from exports.
"This merger is a gateway to an exciting future," said V. Shankar, a director at Croslands. "Croslands would now be a profit centre at Ranbaxy."
Singh said the company will shortly begin marketing its products in South Africa.
Ranbaxy sells its products in 45 countries and has manufacturing facilities in seven countries.
Shankar said the capital of Ranbaxy would go up to 513 million rupees after the merger from 481 million at present.
In the year to March 31, 1996, Ranbaxy had sales of 8.7 billion rupees and a net profit of 1.3 billion, while Croslands reported turnover of 730.3 million and net profit of 120.7 million.
Ranbaxy's Singh declined to forecast the sales and profits of the merged firm.
